item.title: Iran rejects Trump's proposal to end the war and lays out 5 conditions
item.summary: Iran says no to President Trump's ceasefire plan and publicized a counterproposal that includes safeguards against future attacks on Iran and sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: DHS funding deal on shaky ground as Trump and Democrats both decline to embrace it
item.summary: After weeks of start and stop negotiations between Congressional Democrats and the White House, there's an emerging proposal to fund the majority of DHS and tackle ICE enforcement funding separately.

item.title: Savannah Guthrie's first interview since mother Nancy vanished: 'I imagine her terror'
item.summary: Nearly two months after Nancy Guthrie disappeared, her daughter Savannah discusses the toll on her family in an emotional interview with her Today show colleague Hoda Kotb.

item.title: Jury orders Meta and Google to pay woman $3 million in social media addiction trial
item.summary: The verdict marks the end of the first-ever jury trial over whether tech giants should be held accountable for social media addiction. It may influence the outcome of 2,000 other pending lawsuits.

item.title: At the Legacy Museum, facing America's racist past is a path, not a punishment
item.summary: "There is an America that is more free — where there's more equality, where there is more justice, where there is less bigotry — and I think it's waiting for us," says lawyer Bryan Stevenson.

item.title: Yep, a mom's COVID shot during pregnancy protects her baby, a large study finds
item.summary: A 3-year study published in Pediatrics examined newborns in Norway. It found a clear benefit for the baby when mom gets a COVID vaccination during pregnancy.

item.title: They gave her business a lifeline, then froze all her money
item.summary: A murky corner of the financial world is now the fastest-growing source of funding for small businesses. One state, Connecticut, had given these lenders unusual power. That may be about to change.

item.title: For the first time in more than 1,400 years, Church of England gets a woman leader
item.summary: A new archbishop of Canterbury has been installed in a historic ceremony. Sarah Mullally is the 106th person to hold the job, and the first woman.

item.title: A leadership vacuum adds to strains on the CDC
item.summary: Low morale, staff turnover and budget issues have sapped the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The administration is expected to soon name a new director, who will have their hands full.

item.title: A 92-year-old judge will take on the Maduro case. What do we know about him?
item.summary: Former Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro heads to court again this week. The judge overseeing this case is longtime federal Judge Alvin Hellerstein. At 92 years old, Hellerstein is older than the average age of a federal judge by more than 20 years.
